summary: npm package used as jsDelivr CDN vehicle for browser redirect script
details: px8my@1.0.40 ships a single browser-side script (px.js) whose sole behavior is to inject a fullscreen iframe pointing to https://mfmz.jwnrri.cn/H.html into any page that embeds it via jsDelivr. The tarball also contains update_px8my.sh, a maintainer workflow that rotates the destination domain, bumps the package version, runs npm publish, and then purges the jsDelivr CDN cache at purge.jsdelivr.net/npm/px8my/px.js so the new redirect target propagates immediately. There are no preinstall/install/postinstall/prepare lifecycle hooks and the main entry uses document/DOM APIs that throw in Node, so `npm install px8my` and `require('px8my')` in a Node environment do not execute the redirect. The package abuses the npm registry and the jsDelivr CDN as a mutable redirect-distribution channel for third-party websites that hotlink the script; the harm surface is those websites' browser visitors, not developers or build systems installing the package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
